missing_requirements.requirement: Task B brief required design 9: honest terminal disposition and failure reporting; required design 5: native failure diagnostics.
missing_requirements.finding: L01: a fatal native source failure already recorded by the production reader can be followed by terminal=quit, window_closed or deadline and a normal return from run_preview. The nonzero native_exit and stderr are retained, but the overall terminal disposition and CLI success status do not identify the failed source. This is a terminal-status reconciliation gap, not a claim that all native diagnostics are lost.

logic_errors.title: An already-observed native failure can be reported as a normal session termination
logic_errors.explanation: The frame reader records fatal framing/EOF/timeout errors independently. run_preview observes them only when it calls next_frame again. If the child fails during the current detector/packing/display operation, q/Escape, window close or the loop deadline can end the session before another next_frame call. Finalization reads native_exit but never reconciles capture.error or an unexpected pre-cleanup child exit with terminal or primary. Consequently the module can return successfully after the source has failed. The parent-observed successful 60-second session does not contradict this fault-path reproduction.

reproduction.method: Executed production OwnedCapture and run_preview with an ordinary Python subprocess as the synthetic binary-pipe producer. The producer emitted a valid built-in BGRA handshake and one >dI frame, then waited on an inherited synchronization pipe. An injected detector released that pipe, waited for producer exit 7 and waited until the production capture.error contained EOFError before returning. GUI operations were inert injected methods. Model/path admission, hashing, native binding verification and pixel rendering were replaced only to avoid any real model, build, camera, GUI or file operations. The production reader, queue, next_frame, preview-loop decisions and cleanup were not replaced.
reproduction.stderr: The three fault cases retained 'native stderr tail: synthetic native fault'.
reproduction.execution: All corrected focused probes exited 0 after printing their observations. An initial probe-only string-escaping error caused a synthetic-child SyntaxError; it was corrected before these observations and is not counted as a product failure.

logic_errors.required_change: Reconcile a capture failure or unexpected child exit that occurred before owned shutdown with the final session outcome, including normal quit/window-close/deadline paths. Preserve the original failure and cleanup attempts; keep deliberate termination of a healthy owned child distinct from unexpected native failure. Add deterministic regressions for these three ordering cases and the healthy-quit control.

logic_errors.title: Thread-start acquisition failure aborts pipe cleanup and replaces the primary exception
logic_errors.explanation: Both Thread objects are published on self before start() succeeds. Constructor rollback calls close(), which unconditionally joins every non-None thread. Joining a never-started thread raises RuntimeError. This exits the finally block before either stdout or stderr is closed and replaces the intended capture diagnostic with the join exception. _closed has already been set, so another close() cannot complete cleanup. The specifically owned child was terminated and reaped in both reproductions: this finding concerns open pipe handles and failed rollback/diagnostic semantics, not an observed surviving camera process.

reproduction.method: Injected RuntimeError('synthetic thread start failure') at threading.Thread.start for each named production thread in turn, while using the real OwnedCapture constructor/close and a synthetic Python pipe child. Native binding verification alone was bypassed. The frame-reader case received a valid handshake before its thread start was faulted. No real camera, GUI, model, compiler or filesystem writes were involved.

observed.message: cannot join thread before it is started
cannot join thread before it is started

reproduction.execution: Probe exited 0 after recording both cases. The harness explicitly closed the remaining synthetic handles afterward.

logic_errors.required_change: Track successful thread acquisition or guard joining unstarted threads. Ensure pipe closes are attempted even if a thread join or another teardown step fails, preserve the original acquisition error, and do not make incomplete cleanup permanently non-retryable. Cover failure of each thread start through the production constructor.
